claims.claim_vi: Multithreading lets one program execute multiple tasks concurrently; threads are lightweight units of execution sharing process resources such as memory; it brings synchronization, communication and race-condition complexity.
claims.verified_by: Source body read from the pinned commit; the statement is in the source text.

claims.claim_vi: Producer-Consumer uses producer and consumer threads with a blocking queue as the buffer between them.
claims.verified_by: Source body read from the pinned commit; the statement is in the source text.

claims.claim_vi: A thread pool reuses worker threads, removes thread creation and destruction overhead and suits many short-lived tasks.
claims.verified_by: Source body read from the pinned commit; the statement is in the source text.

claims.claim_vi: A promise holds the eventual result and a future gives access to it; suited to long-running operations without blocking the main thread.
claims.verified_by: Source body read from the pinned commit; the statement is in the source text.

claims.claim_vi: Monitor object allows one thread at a time to access or modify a shared resource within an object, preventing race conditions.
claims.verified_by: Source body read from the pinned commit; the statement is in the source text.

claims.claim_vi: A barrier synchronizes a group of threads: each runs until it reaches the barrier and blocks until all have reached it.
claims.verified_by: Source body read from the pinned commit; the statement is in the source text.

claims.claim_vi: A read-write lock lets multiple threads read but only one write at a time; ideal when reads are more frequent than writes.
claims.verified_by: Source body read from the pinned commit; the statement is in the source text.

claims.claim_vi: Python queue implements multi-producer, multi-consumer queues with the required locking semantics.
claims.verified_by: Read from a raw copy at the pinned commit in the URL (a later change to the default branch does not alter it).

claims.claim_vi: ThreadPoolExecutor uses a pool of threads to execute calls asynchronously; Future encapsulates the asynchronous execution of a callable.

design_notes_vi: Sáu mẫu chia thành hai nhóm (chia việc và lấy kết quả; bảo vệ và đồng bộ). Không có mũi tên vì nguồn không nói thứ tự giữa các mẫu. Không dùng ảnh nguồn.
source_deviations: Source gives a short introduction and six patterns in one flat order; the lesson groups them into two sets by what they do.
Library examples (Python and Java) are not in the source and were added from the language documentation, with the caveat that they are not exhaustive.
